extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers preparing an SNSF Ambizione grant application
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an application for the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) Ambizione programme (postdoctoral/early‑career research grant), meeting eligibility, submission and evaluation requirements described by SNSF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctorate / medical studies requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must hold a Doctorate (PhD) or have completed their medical studies (Staatsexamen or equivalent exam).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Ambizione Regulations (article 5) for personal requirements and formal eligibility; the date of the examination or defence of the doctoral thesis is the relevant date for timing calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application timing after doctorate (standard applicants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be submitted no later than four years after completing the doctorate (PhD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The precise periods are calculated on the basis of the relevant submission deadline (3 November 2026). Consult Clause 1.11 of the General implementation regulations for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application timing for medical graduates with clinical work
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who have completed their medical exam and have done clinical work for at least three years after completing their studies may submit an application no later than 9 years after completion of the medical exam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialist certification by the FMH is an advantage; the date of the medical exam is the reference date for timing calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum post‑doctoral research activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Research activities of at least 12 months after the doctorate (PhD), respectively after the medical licence, are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time requirement wording: 'Applicants must have carried out research over a period of at least one year.' This is a hard requirement and cannot be waived (see FAQ: no exceptions for the 12‑month period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Link with Switzerland
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must be of Swiss nationality, or hold a degree from a Swiss higher education institution (master's degree, doctorate, medical diploma, FMH specialist title or equivalent), or have carried out research or clinical work in a Swiss research institution for at least 12 months between the completion of their doctorate or medical diploma and the submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a participation/eligibility requirement for Ambizione; ensure documentation demonstrates Swiss link as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time window extension for special circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: The time window for submission of an Ambizione proposal can be extended if the applicant has suffered a delay due to one of the reasons stated in Clause 1.11 of the General implementation regulations for the Funding Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reasons for extending the time window must be outlined in the application; consult the General implementation regulations for eligible reasons and required documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net academic age considered in evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: The net academic age is taken into account in the evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not confuse net academic age with eligibility time windows: 'No, these two are not to be used synonymously.' For more information see the SNSF net academic age document and CV format guidance; net academic age adjusts for interruptions and non‑scientific work and affects evaluation scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of mobility content and evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: In the statement of mobility, you are expected to justify the choice of the research institution and to present your past and planned mobility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The content of the document 'will be part of the evaluation.' Follow the statement of mobility form and guidelines; make a clear case for why the chosen host is beneficial for the project and career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reapplication limit after rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants whose request for an Ambizione grant was rejected may submit one further application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan applications accordingly; you have one additional attempt after an unsuccessful application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent SNSF project restrictions (applications under evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot submit an Ambizione proposal if you have an SNSF project under evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you currently have another SNSF application being evaluated, delay Ambizione submission until that evaluation concludes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing/approved SNSF project overlap restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have an approved or ongoing SNSF project, you cannot submit an Ambizione proposal for the same funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check planned funding periods to avoid overlap; this restriction prevents double‑funding for the same period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant coverage and distinction with project grant
rubrics_metrics.description: An Ambizione grant covers the grantee's salary and the funds needed to carry out the project. An Ambizione project grant, however, comprises only project funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be clear which type of grant you apply for and budget accordingly; maximum grant duration is four years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum grant duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambizione grants are awarded for a maximum of four years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan project timeline and deliverables within the four‑year maximum; part‑time arrangements can extend the funded calendar period (see work‑time criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Work time percentage requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can meet the 80% average work time requirement over a longer period than the minimum of one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work time (e.g., 80% FTE) can be averaged over a period longer than one year to satisfy eligibility; follow guidance on calculating work time in the application documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part‑time work while on grant (family care and flexibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Working part‑time (min. 0.8 FTE) while being paid by an SNSF grant is possible. It is possible to plan and submit an application with full‑time employment and reduce to part‑time work due to family care duties and thereby extend the duration of the funding period later on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees may request to change their work‑time percentage at any time after the grant has been awarded; consult rules on minimum FTE and how reducing FTE affects project duration and budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of grant to new research institution
rubrics_metrics.description: If you want to transfer your grant to another institution, including the funds covering your salary, contact the SNSF explaining the reasons for the move as well as its added value for your project or your career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A written request from the grantee should include confirmation letters from the new research institution, and an authorized body of the former institution must acknowledge the change in writing. The SNSF evaluates the request taking into account project feasibility and relevance for your career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant termination on leaving academic research
rubrics_metrics.description: If you take on a new job outside of academic research you must inform the SNSF accordingly; the SNSF terminates the grant and the remaining amount of the grant must be refunded to the SNSF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify SNSF in a timely manner and follow termination/refund procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission platform and account setup
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw up your Ambizione application in accordance with the guidelines and submit it using the online platform mySNF. If you are submitting an application to the SNSF for the first time: register on mySNF and request your user account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request your user account at least five working days before the submission deadline to guarantee timely access. The application website opens three months before the deadline; become familiar with the platform early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the Ambizione guidelines, regulations and evaluation form
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific instructions for the Ambizione evaluation procedure can be found in the Guidelines for submission of an Ambizione application, Ambizione Regulations and the Evaluation form – Ambizione.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult these documents (PDFs) for detailed formatting, CV structure, evaluation criteria and required forms; the evaluation procedure (including phase 1/phase 2 and interview panels) is specified there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation procedure: interviews and panels
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambizione evaluation includes phase 1 results and phase 2 interviews; interviews for phase 2 are held by disciplinary panels (dates listed for SSH, MINT, LS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared for panel interviews if you pass phase 1; check panel composition and scheduled interview dates and tailor presentation to panel expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: No interaction with evaluation body members
rubrics_metrics.description: For the SNSF, interaction between applicants and members of evaluation bodies over applications is not compatible with academic best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not contact evaluation body members about your application; follow official channels and documented procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary measures availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary measures are available such as Mobility grants in projects, Flexibility Grant, Media training, and Gender equality grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explore these additional funding/support options as part of project planning; eligibility and conditions vary and are described in separate documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call‑specific deadlines and project start window
rubrics_metrics.description: For the 2025 call: Call opening 5 August 2025; Submission deadline 4 November 2025; Announcement of phase 1 results beginning of April 2026; Announcement of phase 2 results mid‑July 2026. Earliest possible project start – latest possible project start: 1 September 2026 – 1 September 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to call‑specific timelines for application, interviews and planned project start; check the current call page for exact dates as they change between calls.
